terms.definition: A variable that holds the memory address of another variable. Dereferencing it with `*` reads the value at that address.
An alias for an existing variable. Unlike a pointer, a reference must be bound at initialisation and cannot be reseated.
A function that calls itself. Every recursive function needs a base case, a condition under which it stops recurring, or it runs forever.
A mechanism where a class (the derived class) acquires properties and methods from another (the base class). It is the “is-a” relationship in OOP.
The ability of objects of different types to be used through a common interface. In C++ this is achieved with virtual functions.
Bundling data with the methods that operate on it, and exposing only what the outside world needs. Implemented in C++ via the `private` / `public` access keywords.
A blueprint that lets a function or class operate on multiple types. The compiler generates a concrete version for each type that actually gets used.
A runtime signal that something unusual has happened. Thrown with `throw`, caught with `catch`, and unwinds the call stack until handled.
A special member function called automatically when an object of a class is created. Its job is to bring the object into a valid initial state.
A special member function called automatically when an object goes out of scope or is deleted. Used to release resources the object owns.
A member function declared with the `virtual` keyword. Calls to it resolve at runtime based on the object's actual type, enabling polymorphism.
A class that contains at least one pure virtual function. It cannot be instantiated directly, only inherited from.
A named scope for declarations. Used to avoid name collisions, e.g. `std::cout` vs a hypothetical `mylib::cout`.
A qualifier promising that a variable's value won't be modified through that name. Lets the compiler enforce invariants and unlocks optimisations.
An object that points into a container (vector, list, map, ...) and can be advanced to walk through elements. The STL's universal traversal mechanism.
The Standard Template Library, C++'s built-in collection of generic containers (vector, map, set, ...) and algorithms (sort, find, ...).
Dynamically allocated memory (via `new`) that the program never releases. Over time it consumes resources until the process is restarted.
The region of memory managed automatically by the compiler for local variables and function call frames. Allocation is fast and deallocation is automatic.
The region of memory used for dynamic allocations (`new` / `malloc`). The programmer is responsible for releasing it (`delete` / `free`).
Reading or writing the value at the address a pointer holds. In C++, the unary `*` operator dereferences a pointer.
A pointer that intentionally points to no object (`nullptr`). Dereferencing one is undefined behaviour and typically crashes the program.
The value a function approaches as its input approaches some value. The foundation of calculus, derivatives and integrals are both defined via limits.
The instantaneous rate of change of a function with respect to its input. Geometrically, the slope of the tangent line at a point.
The accumulated total of a function's values over an interval. Geometrically, the signed area between the curve and the axis.
A function is continuous at a point if the limit of the function at that point equals the function's value there. Intuitively: no jumps.
